Testimony of Senator Donna Bailey supporting
LD 79, Resolve, to Rename the Bridge on Main Street Between Biddeford and
Saco the General Wallace H. Nutting Memorial Bridge
Before the Joint Standing Committee on Transportation Thursday, February 27, 2025
Senator Nangle, Representative Crafts, and Esteemed Members of the Joint Standing Committee
on Transportation, my name is Donna Bailey, and I proudly represent Senate District 31, which
includes Buxton, Old Orchard Beach, and Saco. Today, I am pleased to offer testimony in strong
support of LD 79, "Resolve, to Rename the Bridge on Main Street Between Biddeford and Saco
the General Wallace H. Nutting Memorial Bridge."
On August 17 , 2023, the people of Saco woke to the news that a larger-than-life legend was no longer with us. That man was General Wallace H. Nutting, a man who, even if we did not know him personally, we certainly knew of him. In light of his passing, it is fitting that the bill before
you seeks to rename the Main Street Bridge between Biddeford and Saco after an extraordinary man who gave so much to these communities.
General Nutting had deep roots in Saco. He attended schools here, and then he joined the Maine
State National Guard at the age of 14, serving from 1942 to 1944. Shortly after graduation from West Point Military Academy, he married Jane Anne Walker in the First Parish Congregational Church in Saco, where they first met when he was 12 years old. They were married for 72 years until Jane's death in 2022. They enjoyed a lifetime of love and marriage that took this military couple across the country and around the world. It all started in Saco.
General Nutting had an impressive career in the military, spanning the Korean War, the Vietnam
War, and beyond, which my colleague and the bill's sponsor Rep. Malon, will describe in detail. In my testimony, I want to highlight General Nutting's contributions and service to the broader
Saco community and the state of Maine.
In I985, General Nutting retired from the military and returned to Maine. He took his leadership skills from the battlefield to the boards of several notable non-profits and organizations. He became a member of the Maine Cancer Research and Education Foundation, the York County
YMCA Board, and the Pine Tree Council of Boy Scouts of America. He was an active member
of the First Parish Congregational Church. He was also a founding member (and Chairman) of
the University of Southern Maine's Senior College Board.
l

Through this service and volunteerism, he demonstrated an exemplary dedication to his family,
family, neighbors, and strangers. He belonged to that increasingly rare and distinguished class of individuals who can only be described as civic leader, educator, soldier, and statesman.
In his lifetime, General Nutting built bridges between the people he led, hailing as they did from
different cultures, states, and nations. He also connected the individuals within the community he gave so much of himself to. With this renaming, his legacy and memory continue to build bridges today, binding our communities together and reminding us that we all have a stake in one
another's success and well-being.
Thank you for your time. I urge the Committee to vote Ought to Pass on LD 79.
Donna Bailey
State Senator, Senate District 31
Buxton, Old Orchard Beach, and Saco

Senator Nangle, Representative Crafts, and Members of the Joint Standing Committee on
Transportation. My name is Henry Ingwersen and I proudly represent the people of Senate
District 32 which includes Arundel, Biddeford, Dayton, Hollis and Lyman. I'm here today in support of LD 79, Resolve to Rename the Bridge on Maine Street Between Biddeford and Saco
the General Wallace H. Nutting Memorial Bridge.
This legislation is quite simple. It seeks to recognize and honor the distinguished service and contributions of General Wallace Nutting, a native of Maine whose military career and leadership left a lasting impact on our state and our nation. General Nutting dedicated his life to
serving this country. Nutting's career began after attending West Point Military Academy. He graduated in 1950 in the last class of Cavalry Officers. Wallace saw combat in the Korean War and received the Silver Star and the Soldier's Medal. The latter was for rescuing a wounded Korean woman from a minefield. In his many years of military service, General Nutting exemplified the values of duty, integrity and service. The Division of Support Command Corrnnander said of him "I have not served with

General Nutting was a true believer in Biddeford's downtown. He did not stand for the invisible line between the cities of Saco and Biddeford. Testimony of Rep. Marc Malon presenting
LD 79, Resolve, to Rename the Bridge on Main Street Between Biddeford and
Saco the General Wallace H. Nutting Memorial Bridge
Before the Joint Standing Committee on Transportation
Senator Nangle, Representative Crafts, and honorable members of the Joint Standing Committee on
Transportation, my name is Marc Malon, and I proudly represent House District 133, which is part of the great City of Biddeford. I am here today to present my bill, LD 79, Resolve, to Rename the Bridge on
Main Street Between Biddeford and Saco the General Wallace H. Nutting Memorial Bridge.
Bridge 3423 connects Main Street in Biddeford at Mechanics Park to Main Street in Saco on Factory
Island, and has a long and symbolic history for botl1 of our communities. LD 79 would name this bridge
after a man who himself represents a bridge between the two cities.
Born and raised in Saco, Wallace Nutting joined the Maine National Guard at age 14 before enrolling at West Point Military Academy, where he graduated in 1950. Thus began a long and distinguished military
career where he was highly decorated for his valor in combat in Korea and Vietnam. He retired from military service in 1985 as the Commander in Chief of the Southern Command. He and his wife Jane, whom he met in Saco when they were both 12, then moved to Biddeford.
In 2003, General Nutting -- at the urging of many community leaders -- ran for Mayor of Biddeford and won. He was re-elected without opposition in 2005, ultimately serving four years as our mayor. His tenure was well-regarded for his professional execution of his duties, for helping to sow the seeds of what would become Biddeford's downtown renaissance, and for the civility which serves as a lesson for all of
us in politics.
Upon leaving office, the president of the Biddeford-Saco Chamber of Commerce said "General Nutting has set the bar to a new, higher level. He has done it by deeds, not words. He has led by example, and his
legacy will be one of outstanding achievement."
Recently, Biddeford and Saco jointly held a ceremony commemorating a dark moment -- the time in 1924
when the Ku Klux Klan attempted to march i11to Biddeford to harass our Franc0~American Catholic

Attached to my testimony are resolutions from both City Councils, both of which passed unanimously.
LD 79 is cosponsored by the entire Biddeford-Saco legislative delegation, and endorsed by both
Biddeford Mayor Marty Grohman and Saco Mayor Jodi MacPhail. At a time of intense polarization, I encourage us all to remember the example of civility and honor and service set by General Wallace Nutting, and I urge the committee to support this resolve. Thank you for your time and consideration.

Testimony of Meghan Russo Maine Department of Transportation
Before the 132"" Legislature, Joint Standing Committee on Transportation
Neither For Nor Against
LD 79, Resolve, to Rename the Bridge on Main Street Between Biddeford and Saco the
General Wallace H. Nutting Memorial Bridge
Senator Nangle, Representative Crafts and distinguished members of the Joint Standing
Committee on Transportation, I am Meghan Russo, Director of Government Affairs at MaineDOT. MaineDOT is neither for nor against LD 79.
MaineDOT considers the naming of bridges, roadways, and other state transportation infrastructure to be within the purview of the Legislature. Simply put, we build them and you name them. Accordingly, we generally do not take positions on so-called "naming bills." However, we usually submit written testimony regarding whether the particular infrastructure under consideration has been named before, and if so what those name(s) are. In this case, we are not aware of any previous legislatively~sanctioned names for this bridge. MaineDOT's
current inventory number for this structure is 3423.
Thank you.
